revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.subtitle: What the installation has billed, collected and is owed.
revenue.loadFailed: The revenue figures could not be loaded.
revenue.noBooks: Nothing has been billed yet, in any currency.
revenue.collectedCaption: Cash received this period, after refunds
revenue.outstandingCaption: Owed right now, whenever it was billed
revenue.runRateNeedsMoreHistory: {{days}} days is too short to scale from — the figure would say more about the window than about the business.
revenue.collectionRatioCaption: This period only. Cash may settle invoices billed earlier.
revenue.collectionRatioUndefined: Nothing was billed this period, so there is nothing to measure against.
revenue.collectionRatioOver: More was collected than billed this period — arrears from earlier periods settled.
revenue.companiesBehindCaption: With at least one overdue invoice
revenue.asOf: Read at {{moment}}. Standing is refreshed by a scheduled sweep, so it can be a little older.
revenue.runRateTrailing: Revenue recognised over the last 30 days
revenue.runRateScaled: Scaled to 30 days from a {{days}}-day window

invoices.title: Invoices
invoices.subtitle: Every document, across every company.
invoices.searchFailed: The search could not be run.
invoices.moreOnAnotherPage: Matches in this currency are on another page.
invoices.totalsDescribeTheFilter: Totals cover everything matched, not just this page.
invoices.outstandingMeaning: What is still owed. Drafts, withdrawn documents and written-off debts count as nothing — nobody is chasing them.
invoices.loadFailed: This invoice could not be loaded.
invoices.exportFailed: The export could not be produced.
invoices.exportTruncated: The export stops at {{cap}} rows; {{total}} match. Narrow the filters to get the rest.
invoices.cancelHelp: For a document that should never have existed. It keeps its number, and the receivable is reversed. A partly wrong invoice is corrected with a credit note instead.
invoices.cancelBlockedPaid: Money has been applied to this invoice. Reverse the allocation first, or issue a credit note.
invoices.creditHelp: For an invoice that was too high. The invoice keeps saying what it said; the credit note says what was given back, and both documents survive for anybody reconciling them.
invoices.writeOffHelp: We billed correctly and will not be paid. The invoice stays overdue and unpaid, which is true — what changes is that we stop chasing it, and the receivable becomes bad debt.

payments.title: Payments
payments.subtitle: Money in, and where each amount went.
payments.pickACompany: Choose a company to see the payments it has made.
payments.none: No payments recorded for this company.
payments.receivedAtHelp: The day the money actually arrived, not today.
payments.referenceHelp: The bank reference or cheque number, so this can be matched against a statement.
payments.amountHelp: In the company's own billing currency.
payments.recordHelp: For money that arrived outside the payment providers — a transfer, a cheque. It lands as credit on the account; applying it to an invoice is a separate step, so a mistake here is recoverable.
payments.allocationsHelp: Every application of money to a document, including the ones that were later undone.
payments.noAllocations: No money has been applied to invoices yet.
payments.reverseHelp: The money goes back to the account as credit and the invoice is owed again. The original application stays on the record — it happened.
payments.refundableHelp: What is left after refunds already issued. Worked out by the server, which knows the whole history.

ledger.title: Customer ledger
ledger.subtitle: Every movement, in the order it happened, with the balance carried down.
ledger.pickACompany: Choose a company to run its account down.
ledger.loadFailed: The statement could not be loaded.
ledger.broughtForward: Brought forward from the previous page
ledger.noEntries: No entries in this account for this period.
ledger.reconstructedHelp: This entry was reconstructed from history rather than written at the time, so it is weaker evidence than the rows around it.
ledger.trialBalanceHelp: One set of books per currency. Nothing converts between them, so there is no combined total.

collections.title: Collections
collections.subtitle: Who is behind, how far, and what happens next.
collections.runHelp: Marks invoices overdue, sends the notices that are due today and suspends anybody who has run out of notices. The same job the scheduler runs — this only brings it forward.
collections.nothingOutstanding: Nothing is outstanding in any currency.
collections.whoIsBehindHelp: Amounts are in each company's own billing currency and are never added together.
collections.everybodyIsCurrent: Every company is up to date.
collections.exemptHelp: The sweep will never suspend this company on its own. A person has to decide.
collections.exemptionHelp: Some customers must never be cut off by a scheduled job — a government tenant, or one mid-way through a procurement. Exempting them keeps the notices going but leaves the suspension to a person.
collections.exemptionReasonHelp: Recorded on the audit trail. Six months from now this is the only explanation anybody will have.

company.title: Company billing
company.subtitle: What this customer owes, what they are running up, and what they have been billed.
company.loadFailed: This company's billing could not be loaded.
company.noInvoices: This company has not been invoiced yet.
company.issuedOnly: Issued invoices only, matching what the customer sees.
